What are some small things that may not be obvious to a new Vegan that would be good to know.

Hey, congratulations on going vegan!! :)

Being busy and not having time to plan out food can be a problem. Until next week when you'll have more time to cook, I would just suggest taking lots of healthy snacks with you to work, like nuts, energy bars, that kind of things. And just get used to eating more. Eating vegan for me meant taking in more food to get enough calories.

If you don't have a lot of time, I would suggest convenience foods (in the frozen section of your market), until you can start cooking.

You sound like you're in the UK, so I don't know what you've got there, but there's lots of different vegan choices here now in the US in regular grocery stores (like Amy's and Gardein). They can be expensive though, so I only buy those things when I just don't have any time at all (or I'm feeling lazy). ;)

Anyway, good luck and welcome!

I have two tubs of Pumpkin seeds and dried fruit and other nuts in them that I snack on during the day amongst the fruit that is usually on set. Thanks for the tips :) But ill make sure I bring a few more extra snacks!

My biggest suggestion after a few years vegan:

  • Costs! Some of the popular vegan things can be very expensive. (IE meat replacements etc.)

  • Learn to make everything your self. Don't be afraid to experiment and fail.

  • Buy dry items in bulk. Examples: Beans, rice

"Animal-Free" is a really useful phone app that you can use to determine whether or not an ingredient you don't recognize is vegan or not. I've been vegan for over four years and I still use it when I'm unsure about something. Always pack something vegan if you don't know that there will be anything available at work. I travel and usually end up living off of Clif bars.

start with a little food for thought. are you satisfied with food not containing animal products or do you also need for it to be produced in a factory and with equipment that does not handle animal products at all? for example some bread makers have bread that contains milk and other varieties that do not, but they use the same equipment on both.

hummus and "________" is awesome. pre-made, homemade, its all great snack food or addition to any meal. buy a bag of carrots, celery, pita chips, broccoli, whatever you want to dip and go at it.

nuts, avocado, flax seed, wherever you get it, get your fats in.

edamame is delicious, a decent source of protein, can be prepped in the microwave, and is a very easy snack.

find your go to foods and meals and you'll be set.

i found that once i stopped trying to replicate and replace non-vegan food and started enjoying vegan fare the diet became much easier and my options stopped feeling like restrictions.

good luck and welcome to the land of herbivores.

If you're baking and something requires egg you can mix 1tbsp of ground flax seed with 3tbsp water (this will sub one egg). Stir it up and let it sit for 5 minutes. It works perfectly and is far cheaper than egg replacer.
Don't be afraid of frozen veg. They are just as healthy as fresh, and you don't have to worry about spoilage.
McDonald's fries aren't vegan (natural beef flavoring) but, Wendys, BK, and Carl's Jr,/Hardees have vegan fries. For when you eat out with nonveg friends.

If you ever really want something like cheese, milk, or ice cream there's a soy version for them. To be honest the vegan alternatives aren't that good. I compare it to a heroin addict switching to methadone. Eventually you'll probably give them all up but its a good substitute in the mean time.

I got my first tattoo a few years ago. It is supposed to be a bearded dragon, a memorial to a pet that passed away.

Frankly, it looks awful...It looks like a scratcher did it.

I was just curious if any of you have/had a tattoo you don't like, and if you felt bad about covering it up.

Here's mine, and the exact image I gave as a reference....I didn't want the exact image but I didn't want a spiky frog with down syndrome, either...http://imgur.com/a/IKj2u

Every time I look at it I cringe...this was supposed to be something to remember my pet by...it's just...bad. The artist had done some really awesome stuff, too so in my opinion that makes it even worse.

Thoughts?

I don't particularly want to share about where I got it. The other guys at the shop were great, and the guy who did this had an awesome portfolio...It's like he just didn't care about this...
Ever gotten a tattoo you were unhappy with? If you got it covered, did you feel bad about it?

First off I don't think you tattoo is terrible. He could certainly be touched up and reworked by another artist, probably someone who works with portraits and also experienced in coverups.

But yea, I had some bad tattoos just recently covered up. When I say bad I mean it, like no touching up could ever fix the bad decision I made on my arm.

I got the first when I was 13 this was probably 1993, I knew some older kids from skipping class and at the time and one of them happened to be pretty decent at drawing, he had just started dabbling in tattoos with a crude homemade gun fashioned from a old tape deck motor, allen wrench, bic pen and guitar string. One day we were in his apartment living room and he's giving out free tattoos, so unsanitary... ugh, looking back it's embarrassing to even recollect... Sadly I got a skull with devil horns that day. I thought I was the baddest kid in the world, I showed it to all my friends at middle school, I was so tuff for those few weeks. I had to of course hide it from my mom as she would kill me.

So about 6 months later I'm still hanging out with this group of older (bad) kids, slowly corrupting of course. End up in a tattoo shop cause a buddy's getting a tattoo with his new fake ID, one of the artist in the shop asks me if I'm there to get a tattoo. I pointed at some random flash on the wall and said how about this? He sat me down, looked at the skull on my arm, lined up the stencil and never asked to see my ID. 90$ later I walked out with a red eyed wizard under my devil horned skull.

I lived with those bad tattoos till just about 4 months ago when my sleeve finally started covering it all away, I'm so happy to see them go. I know they're memories in the flesh, but I don't need to see them to remember anymore.

It certainly isn't the worst tattoo I've ever seen, so I can be thankful for that.

I'm just embarrassed by it. I get asked if it's a frog a lot and I have no idea why it's sticking it's tongue out...I just want something I can be more proud of. Something that doesn't make me hate wearing shorts, you know?

yep, I know exactly. I would only buy loose fitting t-shirts with longer sleeves to make sure no part of that stupid wizard stuck out. When a portion showed and someone would grab my sleeve to pull it up and see what is was I would just cringe and freeze.. currently I like wearing sleeveless shirts. =)

How do you end up with a tattoo you don't like? Don't they draw it out for you before it get's tattooed?

I ask because I want to get one but this worries me.

Depends on what the tattoo is. With portraits like this they'd usually just work from the photo, because there's not really much point in spending however many hours redrawing something that you already have right there in front of you.

Generally with other designs they'd draw it out first, but sometimes artists freehand the design straight onto the skin with markers. They might do that because the placement would make it difficult or impossible to get a stencil on, or if they're filling a gap and want to make sure it'll fit, or some artists just prefer to do things that way. Most would have the design ready in advance and use stencils, though.

My artist worked from a photo and both drew it out and stenciled it on before we started. Made me a lot more confident.

Honestly, I'd be a bit concerned if the dude(tte) just freehand drew it on my skin.

He did draw it out first and it looked WAY better. He transferred it to my skin and started working on it.

At first it didn't really hurt at all, but as he got closer to my ankle I almost couldn't take it. Call me a baby if you will, I don't have a high pain tolerance, I was too busy biting on a paper towel to pay much attention to what he was doing to my leg. Mistake number one.

He got lazy. He didn't even do half of the scales and spikes that were transferred onto me. I wish I had a picture of what he transferred. If you saw that and then looked at what's on my leg you'd be appalled.

Once he was done I had no idea how much time had passed. While he was tattooing he didn't let me get up at all. After telling people about that they've said that isn't normal at all and most artists will give you a break if you need it...anywho, at that point I was just in pain and wanted to go home. I looked at it when he was done, but I didn't really look at it. Mistake number two.

Also, as my own skills in art grew, I started to dislike it more and more. Now I'm pretty much disgusted by it.
Oh, now I can see how that could easily happen. For what it's worth, I don't think your tattoo is that bad. I hope you find a way to turn it into something you can be proud of.

Yeah. If you do go to get a tattoo I recommend looking at the artist's portfolio and paying attention to what they're doing while they tattoo you instead of crying like a baby like I did. XD

Not saying I wont cry next time but I'll multitask.

It happens more often with text based tattoos. I went through a weird phase early college where I was really into The Notebook. I decided to get the quote "Science only goes so far and then comes God" tattooed...in Latin...on my upper arm ( I actually just posted it to this subverse lol). Flash forward 2 years. Am now an Atheist who hates how corny is old tattoo looked. Just got it covered (luckily wasn't too hard to cover).

Just be smart :) If it's a picture you probably won't end up hating it. If its text or an inspiration quote think twice...or three times.
It doesn't look that bad, but I understand why you would want to get it covered/changed. If you got more cartoony stuff around it it would look better, it that appeals to you.

I have a pretty big one on my arm that I'm getting lasered. Don't feel bad about it in the slightest. I got it within a month of turning 18, by a guy a friend recommended to me. It's pretty bad, the lines are wonky and it wasn't designed very well in the first place. When I started getting good tattoos on the same arm a few years later, it just looked even worse by comparison. I'd much rather have something good there.

I agree that your tattoo probably isn't beyond saving. I don't know how realistic another artist would be able to make it because there are some pretty harsh lines there, you might have to go with something slightly stylised, but it'd definitely be worth getting someone to have a look at it. It's a real pity about the first artist, but you do get people like that. In the studio I apprenticed in we had a guy who'd do guest spots with us on a pretty regular basis. When his work was good it was great and he's won loads of awards for it, but I saw him do some shockingly bad tattoos when he wasn't in the mood or if he took a dislike to the customer.

It kind of makes me mistrust tattoo artists now, just a little bit. It's so not okay for them to do shoddy work on people. Even though it can be covered/lasered, it'll still be there for a while and make the person feel bad about it.

Saddest part is he traced the reference...there's no excuse for it to be this bad if he did that, in my honest opinion.

I've drawn up a cover for it myself, tracing areas from the original reference so it'll match up properly. http://i59.tinypic.com/fapft5.jpg That I could be proud of. I'm going to a local parlor today at some point to see what it'll cost to do.

Honestly, now that I looked at your tattoo, it could definitely be worse. Nice drawing, so you're set on realism? I think what you've got now would make a sick Japanese traditional or maybe kinda cartooned out?

Either way, your cover-up idea looks good!
